holding_summary: The case turns entirely on where the defendant's domicil was located for purposes of jurisdiction over a suit on a note and mortgage debt; it does not involve letting, lodging, or boarding of any dwelling.
notes: Pure domicil/jurisdiction dispute (occasional absence from parish while attending to plantation business); no lodging, boarding, or short-term letting issue present.

holding_summary: Ordinary commercial lease dispute over a store: no new lease contract was formed when the tenant refused the landlord's renewal terms but continued occupying, so the tenant owed rent only for the period actually occupied, on a month-to-month tacit reconduction theory.
notes: Lease dispute concerns a store (commercial premises), not a dwelling or rooms let for lodging/boarding; doctrine is ordinary lease/tacit reconduction law, off-topic.

holding_summary: The plaintiff had kept a boarding house for mechanics as her own thriving business before the defendant took over its management; the court affirmed a jury verdict awarding her compensation, at roughly a common servant's wage, for her services managing the house and the wear on her furniture.

quotes.text: For the faithful and incessant services, in attending to the management of an humble boarding house, which fall to the lot of a female ; for the wear and tear of her furniture, the jury have believed that she is entitled to a sum which does not exceed what a common black servant would be allowed, at the ordinary rate, about ten dollars per month.

For the faithful and incessant services, in attending to the management of an humble boarding house, which fall to the lot of a female ; for the wear and tear of her furniture, the jury have believed that she is entitled to a sum which does not exceed what a common black servant would be allowed, at the ordinary rate, about ten dollars per month.

notes: Court treats plaintiff's boarding-house business (kept for mechanics, well supplied with furniture) as a legitimate ordinary enterprise entitled to legal protection/compensation; no discussion of boarders' individual duration or the legal character (lease/license/lodging) of their occupancy, so characterization left null.

holding_summary: Holds that a lessor's privilege for rent under a one-year lease payable monthly extends to arrearages beyond the last month's rent, not merely the current month.
notes: Purely a lessor's-privilege/lien doctrine case concerning arrearages on a tenement lease; no facts about a dwelling let for lodging or boarding purposes.

holding_summary: Holds that a provisional seizure for rent cannot be sustained where the petition and evidence fail to show the defendant occupied the premises as lessee or sub-lessee, rather than merely as an occupant.
notes: Purely procedural landlord's-privilege/provisional-seizure case; no facts about lodging, boarding, or a dwelling let short-term.

holding_summary: Extensive succession litigation over Isaac Franklin's domicil (Tennessee vs. Louisiana) for community-property purposes, and over the validity under Louisiana law of a testamentary trust bequest to establish an educational seminary; the trust bequest as to Louisiana immovables was annulled as an unrecognized/prohibited tenure.
notes: Long domicil/succession/trust-and-substitution opinion; no content whatsoever regarding letting of rooms, lodging, or boarding houses despite a stray selector match on unrelated Latin domicil text.

holding_summary: Suit to recover slaves under a bill of sale that the court found to be a fraudulent simulation between the plaintiff and her brother-in-law, intended to shield the slaves from creditors; judgment for the defendants who held the slaves under a subsequent bona fide title.
notes: The fact that the plaintiff "kept a boarding house in the interior of the State" is mentioned only in passing, to help establish she lacked means to make the purchase; the boarding-house keeping is not at issue and has no bearing on the case's holding.

holding_summary: Holds that keeping the game of Keno is punishable under the 1835 state anti-gambling statute regardless of whether the stake is furnished by the house or the players, and that the city could not impose its own separate penalty for conduct already made a state offense.
notes: Concerns regulation of gaming houses, not lodging or boarding houses; selector match on 'regulation'/police-power language but subject matter is unrelated.

holding_summary: Holds that ground rents from the city's sale of former commons on perpetual ground rent are legally destined as municipal revenue for police and government purposes, and therefore cannot be seized and sold under an ordinary money judgment against the municipality.
notes: Municipal finance/ground-rent seizure case; no connection to lodging, boarding, or short-term letting of dwellings.

holding_summary: Holds that police juries have power to lay out roads and establish ferries over navigable or non-navigable water-courses, and that the act of sovereignty in laying out a road or ferry creates no warranty or right to indemnity absent an express stipulation.
notes: Road/ferry police-power case unrelated to lodging or boarding houses.

holding_summary: Petitory-action fruits-and-improvements accounting after eviction: a good-faith possessor is entitled to reimbursement for necessary agricultural improvements (clearings, levees, ditches) even those made after judicial demand, and owes fruits only from the date of judicial demand.
notes: Concerns agricultural land possession/improvements after a petitory eviction, not a dwelling let for lodging or boarding.

holding_summary: Holds that a joint owner who has possessed a portion of jointly-owned land nomine proprio and in good faith for more than a year may maintain a possessory action against a co-owner who forcibly disturbs that possession.
notes: Possessory-action dispute between joint owners of a plantation; the plaintiff's renting of the land out to farm tenants is incidental and does not involve dwelling/lodging arrangements.

holding_summary: Holds that a formerly enslaved concubine could not validly receive a donation of promissory notes made or delivered before her emancipation, and that the deceased donor's domicil (a threshold issue for community-property and donation-validity purposes) remained in Louisiana rather than Missouri.
notes: Domicil/donation/concubinage succession dispute; no lodging, boarding, or letting of a dwelling is at issue despite selector match on unrelated domicil-doctrine text.

holding_summary: Upholds a municipal wharfage ordinance charging vessels for mooring as a lawful compensation for port facilities, not an unconstitutional tax, duty, or tonnage charge under the U.S. Constitution.
notes: Municipal wharfage/constitutional-commerce-clause case; wholly unrelated to lodging or boarding houses.

holding_summary: Holds that a police jury's location of a public road across a planter's land is subject to judicial review, and must be laid out with as little injury to the landowner as is compatible with the public interest.
notes: Road-location/police-jury power case, unrelated to lodging or boarding-house regulation.

holding_summary: Holds that a slave-yard keeper's expenses for boarding, clothing, and medical attendance furnished to attached slaves constitute a privilege on the slaves themselves as movable property.
notes: "Boarding" here refers to custodial care/maintenance of attached slaves as chattel property at a slave-yard, not to compensated human lodging or letting of a dwelling; outside project scope.

holding_summary: Holds that attaching creditors must be satisfied in the order their attachments were levied, and that the landlord's privilege for rent due takes preference over an attaching creditor's claim to the proceeds of a store's stock of goods.
notes: Commercial store rent/attachment-priority dispute; no dwelling, lodging, or boarding arrangement involved.

holding_summary: Holds that a tenant whose leased house is temporarily inconvenienced by an adjoining owner's lawful demolition and rebuilding of a party wall cannot dissolve the lease or abandon the premises, but is entitled only to a proportional reduction in rent for the period of inconvenience.
notes: Ordinary year-long house lease dispute about a landlord's structural/party-wall obligations; not about short-term letting, lodging, or boarding-house practice.
